architecture.mechanism: Digital twin modeling of induction motors enables precise data acquisition and analysis to isolate the specific electromagnetic or mechanical loss component causing anomalous no-load heating, despite balanced resistance and stable supply voltage.
architecture.intervention: Construct a digital twin of the 3-phase induction conveyor drive motor using real-time data acquisition of no-load current, voltage harmonics, and temperature to model and identify the exact loss mechanism (such as excessive core loss from high-frequency supply harmonics or bearing friction) responsible for the thermal overload trip.
architecture.expected_effect: The digital twin will pinpoint the root cause of the no-load overheating by comparing acquired operational data against the idealized digital model, allowing targeted correction of the identified fault without replacing the motor.
architecture.falsification_test: Run the motor on a known pure sinusoidal 400V supply with verified low harmonic distortion; if the thermal overload still trips after 20 minutes of no-load running, the hypothesis that supply harmonics or external electrical anomalies are the cause is falsified, proving an internal mechanical or magnetic defect independent of supply quality.
